records.why: Evaluating 3 ^ (60 << 3) ^ (8 << 6) yields 3 ^ 480 ^ 512 = 995 (0x3E3), confirming the test expectation.

records.claim: A 64-bit float value with Val[63:55] equal to 0x80 shifted to digest bits [11:3] produces digest 0x400.
records.why: Figure 6(b) specifies shifting Val[63:55] to digest bit 3 with bits [2:0] zeroed, yielding 0x80 << 3 = 0x400.

records.claim: A 4-bit condition code nibble 0b1011 (0xB) replicated three times produces 12-bit digest 0xBBB.
records.quote: For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 defines replicating the four flag bits three times, which for 0xB results in 0xBBB.

records.claim: An entry's decay counter invalidates the entry after 256 decoded instructions without new writes.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies invalidation after 256 subsequent decoded instructions.

records.claim: The register with highest usefulness in a bank is selected, and its WT sum is scaled by 2.5 when usefulness is positive.
records.quote: Unlike the existing components, this component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available and forwards it to the second table.
records.why: Section 4.2 defines selecting the most useful available register within the bank to forward to prediction tables.

records.claim: Completed register digests remain valid across pipeline flushes, enabling immediate correlation after squashes.
records.quote: However, we found that by the time a branch resolves and its misprediction is revealed, many in-flight instructions have already finished execution, thereby enlarging the set of values visible to the predictor when it restarts, and this fact can be exploited.
records.why: Section 4.2 describes how instructions completing before or during flush remain available to enlarge the visible digest set upon restart.

records.claim: The predict algorithm is triggered at branch prediction lookup time for conditional branches.
records.quote: Whenever the branch predictor queries the table, any entry whose valid bit is set forwards its digest to the register-value components in the SC for prediction.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that available digests are forwarded to the register components whenever the predictor queries the table.

records.claim: The algorithm iterates over 8 banks, computing 3 UT indices per bank to evaluate register usefulness.
records.quote:
Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
    Their outputs go to a Sigma producing "9 regs useful (skewed)".
    That vector feeds a block labelled "largest", whose output is labelled
    "Most useful in this bank."
records.why: Figure 5(c) documents the 3 usefulness tables UT0, UT1, UT2 evaluated per bank to find the most useful register.

records.claim: During prediction, one valid register in each bank is randomly sampled for potential training update.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies that if several registers were available within the bank, one is randomly selected for the update.

records.claim: The chosen register digest and PC index 3 prediction weight tables (WT0 512 entries, WT1 256 entries, WT2 128 entries).
records.quote:
Selected digest plus PC form the input labelled "PC + reg. digest",
    hashed into "h0", "h1", "h2".
    Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1",
    "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) details that PC and the selected digest hash into h0, h1, h2 to index WT0 (512), WT1 (256), and WT2 (128).

records.claim: The bank weight sum is multiplied by 2.5 when selected register usefulness is positive, and gated to 0 otherwise.
records.quote: Reading: each bank's contribution is scaled by 2.5 when that bank's usefulness is positive and suppressed entirely (x0) when it is not; the eight scaled per-bank contributions are then summed to give sR.
records.why: Figure 5(c) establishes that each bank's contribution is scaled by 2.5 if useful or suppressed to 0 otherwise.

records.claim: The token 'bank' in 'for bank in 0 .. 7:' represents a loop variable iterating over bank indices rather than an undefined function call.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: The component comprises 8 banks indexed 0 through 7.

records.claim: The token 'if' is a standard language conditional control-flow keyword rather than an undefined function call.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: The conditional check implements the selective gating between x0 and x2.5 based on usefulness.

records.claim: The call int32(...) represents an integer type conversion to a 32-bit signed accumulator rather than an undefined helper call.
records.quote: Below all eight banks: a final Sigma, output "sR".
records.why: The scaled bank weight is accumulated into the signed sR sum.

records.claim: The token 'return' in predict represents a standard language return construct returning the prediction tuple.
records.quote: Below all eight banks: a final Sigma, output "sR".
records.why: The predict algorithm returns the computed sR sum to merge into SC LSUM.

records.claim: sR_WT is organized into 8 banks, each containing 3 direct-mapped sub-tables WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), and WT2 (128 entries).
records.quote:
WT: 6 bits x (2^7 + 2^8 + 2^9) x 8 banks = 6 x (128+256+512) x 8 = 43008 bits
      so per bank WT0=512, WT1=256, WT2=128 entries, 6-bit weights.
records.why: Figure 5(c) and Table 3 specify 8 banks of WT0 (512), WT1 (256), WT2 (128) entries.

records.claim: Each WT entry is a 6-bit signed saturating counter in range [-32, 31], totalling 43,008 bits across all banks.
records.why: Table 3 defines the WT structure as 6-bit weights spanning (128 + 256 + 512) * 8 entries.

records.claim: sR_UT comprises 8 banks, each having 3 direct-mapped sub-tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies 3 sub-tables of 8 entries each per bank.

records.claim: Each UT entry contains a vector of 6-bit usefulness counters corresponding to the registers mapped to that bank (9 in bank 0, 8 in banks 1-7), totalling 9,360 bits.
records.quote:
UT: 6 bits x 65 regs x (2^3 + 2^3 + 2^3) = 9360 bits
      so UT0/UT1/UT2 have 8 entries each, and every entry carries one 6-bit
      weight per register of that bank (hence "9x6bit" for bank 0).
records.why: Figure 5(c) and Table 3 establish that each UT entry stores 6-bit weights for all registers in that bank.

records.claim: reg_tracking_table is a direct-mapped table of 65 entries corresponding to logical registers R0 through R64.
records.quote: We use a dedicated table that contains one entry per logical register. Each entry consists of a valid bit and a payload that can hold either a 14-bit tag or a 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 defines the dedicated table containing one entry per logical register.

records.claim: Each entry in reg_tracking_table consists of a 1-bit valid flag, a 14-bit payload, and an 8-bit decay counter, consuming 1,495 bits total.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Table 3 auxiliary data specifies the entry format: valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) across 65 registers.

records.claim: The default number of banks in the sR component is 8.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly establishes the 8-bank organization.

records.claim: The default number of entries in WT0 is 512 entries per bank.
records.quote:
Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1",
    "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies 512 entries for WT0.

records.claim: The default number of entries in WT1 is 256 entries per bank.
records.quote:
Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1",
    "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies 256 entries for WT1.

records.claim: The default number of entries in WT2 is 128 entries per bank.
records.quote:
Three prediction weight tables: "512 ent. WT0", "256 ent. WT1",
    "128 ent. WT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies 128 entries for WT2.

records.claim: The default number of entries per UT sub-table is 8.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies 8 entries for each usefulness sub-table.

records.claim: The usefulness multiplier applied to useful bank weight sums is 2.5.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies a 2.5x scaling multiplier for positive usefulness bank outputs.
